title: Security Trading Policy and Insider Trading Policy

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: The Board; directors and company secretary of any subsidiary; any person entitled to receive equity performance rights and/or options under an equity incentive scheme; any Executives; and the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Associated parties
tiers.description: Immediate family (including a spouse (or equivalent) or dependent), family company or trust of a Restricted Person; subject to the same restrictions as the Restricted Person.

definitions.hedging_definition: hedging arrangements include entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities in the Company

windows.start_anchor: 5 business days before the announcement of a dividend or any other capital management initiative that might have a material impact on the share price
windows.end_anchor: announcement of the dividend or capital management initiative

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may from time to time designate further periods of time as a prohibited period. The Board has absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons and/or their associated parties trading in the Company's securities at any time. Confidentiality of such embargoes is not addressed.

rules.detail: No separate derivatives provision. A purchased put and written call over the Company's securities are transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk of holding the securities, so they fall within the absolute hedging ban with no vesting-state or tier carve-out and no clearance route.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not enter into hedging arrangements with respect to securities in the Company (including any shares, options and rights).

rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging arrangements, defined as transactions in financial products that limit the economic risk of holding the Company's securities. Applies regardless of vesting status and extends to associated parties. No clearance or exception route is provided in this section.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not enter into hedging arrangements with respect to securities in the Company (including any shares, options and rights).

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A cash-settled forward or similar arrangement not involving security over the shares would be a general 'dealing' requiring prior written notice to the Company Secretary (who confers with the Chairperson) and observance of blackout periods; if it involves granting security over the shares it would instead be treated as secured financing under 1.11, requiring Board consent.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons are required to notify the Company of intended dealings in the Company's securities, by themselves or their associated parties, prior to such intended dealings.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named or referenced anywhere in the policy.
Securities lending is not named or referenced anywhere in the policy.

CFDs are not named. A CFD over the Company's securities used to limit economic risk is a 'financial product' caught by the absolute hedging ban; a purely directional (long) CFD is not addressed and would fall back to the general dealing notification rule.
rules.evidence: hedging arrangements include entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities in the Company

rules.detail: Margin lending using the Company's securities requires the Board's prior consent, which the Company may make conditional. Expressly covers entering into the arrangement, transferring securities into an existing margin loan account, and selling securities to satisfy a margin call.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not include his or her securities in the Company in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise deal in securities in the Company pursuant to a margin lending arrangement without first obtaining the Board's consent.

rules.detail: General encumbrance (a charge, lien or pledge unconnected to a margin loan) is not separately named. Only encumbrance arising from a margin lending arrangement is addressed, and that requires the Board's prior consent.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not include his or her securities in the Company in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise deal in securities in the Company pursuant to a margin lending arrangement without first obtaining the Board's consent.

rules.detail: Only margin lending is expressly regulated as secured financing; no broader restriction on other secured financing structures is stated. A margin lending arrangement requires prior Board consent, which may be made subject to conditions (e.g. the circumstances in which securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
rules.evidence: The Company may, at its discretion, make any clearance granted in accordance with this section 1.11 conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, in regards to the circumstances in which the securities in the Company may be sold to satisfy a margin call).

rules.detail: No minimum holding period, intention test, or short-term dealing restriction is stated.

clearance.approver: Chairperson, via written notice to and conferral with the Company Secretary
clearance.evidence: Restricted Persons are required to notify the Company of intended dealings in the Company's securities, by themselves or their associated parties, prior to such intended dealings. This should be done by written notice to the Company Secretary... The Company Secretary will confer with the Chairperson in relation to any proposed dealing.

A Restricted Person must not include his or her securities in the Company in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise deal in securities in the Company pursuant to a margin lending arrangement without first obtaining the Board's consent.

exceptions.approver: Chairperson (or another Director where the Chairperson is involved)
exceptions.evidence: clearance may be given for the Restricted Person to sell (but not to purchase) securities in the Company when that person would otherwise be prohibited from doing so ... 'exceptional circumstances' means severe financial hardship

exceptions.approver: Chairperson (or another Director where the Chairperson is involved)
exceptions.evidence: a court order (or court enforceable undertaking), or some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement, to transfer or sell securities in the Company

an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the securities of the entity) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer or pursuant to a scheme of arrangement implemented in accordance with section 411 of the Corporations Act

trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the Shareholders of the Company, such as, a rights issue, a share purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back
the cancellation or surrender of an option under an employee scheme
the purchase of securities or the communication of information pursuant to a requirement imposed by law
undertakings or elections to take up entitlements under a rights issue or other offer (including an offer of securities in lieu of a cash dividend)

exemption_authority: No exemption authority exists for the absolute hedging ban in section 1.10. For margin lending (1.11) and general closed-period dealing, the Board or Chairperson may grant consent/clearance, which may be made conditional; under 1.8, the Chairperson may excuse a sale (never a purchase) in exceptional circumstances, but not while inside information exists.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person must not enter into hedging arrangements with respect to securities in the Company (including any shares, options and rights).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike the margin lending provisions, section 1.10 provides no Board consent or exceptional-circumstances route, so the put and call legs of a funded collar cannot be cleared under any circumstance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company may, at its discretion, make any clearance granted in accordance with this section 1.11 conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, in regards to the circumstances in which the securities in the Company may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a plain loan secured on the shares (without derivatives) is subject to bespoke Board-imposed conditions on when the bank may force-sell collateral, potentially constraining standard default remedies.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Chairperson may not give clearance under the exception in section 1.8 if there is a matter about which there is inside information in relation to securities in the Company ... when the Restricted Person requests clearance or proposes to deal.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A hardship-driven unwind of any collar-adjacent position can only be effected as a sale, never a repurchase, and is unavailable whenever inside information exists.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Board has absolute discretion to place an embargo on Restricted Persons and/or their respective associated parties trading in the Company's securities at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An unannounced Board embargo could block entry, roll or unwind of a collar-related transaction at any time, independent of the scheduled blackout window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Each Restricted Person has a personal responsibility to ensure that his or her 'associated parties' (being immediate family (including a spouse (or equivalent) or dependent), family company or trust) complies with the same respective restrictions as applied to Restricted Persons.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, family trust or family company does not avoid the hedging ban or the margin-loan consent requirement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons are required to notify the Company of intended dealings in the Company's securities, by themselves or their associated parties, prior to such intended dealings.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even outside a scheduled blackout, any dealing connected to a collar (such as the loan itself, or an unwind) must be pre-notified to the Company Secretary and Chairperson.

summary: A funded collar with a bank is not achievable under this policy. Section 1.10 imposes an absolute, unconditional ban on hedging arrangements over the Company's securities (including shares, options and rights), which squarely catches a purchased put and written call, and unlike the margin lending provisions this ban has no Board consent, clearance or exceptional-circumstances mechanism. Separately, section 1.11 permits a margin lending or other secured financing arrangement over the shares only with the Board's prior consent, which may be made conditional, so the loan leg alone could in principle proceed with Board approval, transfers into the margin account and margin-call sales are treated as dealings needing consent, and any forced sale must also respect blackout periods and the absence of inside information. Because the derivative legs are prohibited outright, the funded collar structure as a whole cannot be implemented, even though an unhedged secured loan against vested shares might be approved by the Board on its own conditions. Any residual dealing (e.g. an unwind) still requires prior written notice to the Company Secretary and Chairperson and must avoid the 5-business-day dividend/capital-management blackout and any ad hoc Board embargo.
